stem: How many ways can the letters of the word FACTOR be arranged if each arrangement uses all six letters exactly once?

per_option_rationale.rationale: All 6 letters in FACTOR are distinct. The number of arrangements of n distinct objects is n!, so 6! = 720.
Computed 6! / 2 = 360, as if one letter were repeated twice, but FACTOR has no repeated letter.
Evaluated 5! = 120 instead of 6!, treating the word as having 5 letters.
Evaluated 7! = 5040 instead of 6!, adding an extra letter to the count.

explanation: FACTOR has 6 distinct letters. Arranging n distinct objects gives n! arrangements: 6! = 720.

explanation_sections.punchline: All 6 letters are distinct, so the count is simply 6! = 720.
explanation_sections.approach: Classify as an unrestricted arrangement of distinct objects. Count the letters, confirm none repeat, then write n!. Here n = 6, so 6! = 6 x 5 x 4 x 3 x 2 x 1 = 720.
explanation_sections.lesson: The moment you confirm all letters are distinct, the answer is n!. Division enters only when letters repeat.
explanation_sections.timing: 20-25 s. The trap is dividing by 2 for some imagined repeated letter - scan FACTOR: F, A, C, T, O, R - all distinct.
